summary: Marks the 40th anniversary of the RFC document series with a short reflection. It is a commemorative memo rather than a technical specification.

eli5.summary: The series of internet notes turned forty years old. This note is like a birthday card, looking back at how it began and how it grew.

questions: when did the rfc series start
who was the first rfc editor
subtitle: The RFC Editor marks the 40th birthday of the RFC series and notes what changed in ten years.

tldr.problem: The RFC series reached its 40th anniversary and the RFC Editor wanted to mark it and record changes since the 30th.
tldr.mechanism: The memo recalls RFC 1 and Jon Postel, points back to RFC 2555, and lists changes in organization, funding and process.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational commemoration with no protocol content, and it is updated by RFC 8700.

today: RFC 5540 is an Informational memo that is updated by RFC 8700. The links to RFC 1 and RFC 2555 give the earlier history.

sections.title: RFC 1 and Jon Postel
sections.content:
The first RFC, RFC 1, was published at UCLA forty years before the memo's date of 7 April 2009. The series then held more than 5400 documents, roughly 160,000 pages. It emerged from the US government-funded research that created the ARPANET and later the Internet, and became the main publication vehicle for IETF standards after the IETF formed in the mid-1980s.

For the first 29 years, Jon Postel was the RFC Editor, until his death in October 1998, with substantial help from Joyce K. Reynolds. He worked at USC/ISI from 1978 until 1998 and was also the original IANA.
sections.eli5: One man looked after the collection of Internet books for 29 years, with help from a colleague.

sections.title: Changes Over Ten Years
sections.content:
RFC 2555 marked the 30th anniversary, and the memo says it still holds true. It notes these changes:

  • Joyce Reynolds and Bob Braden formed a small USC/ISI organization to continue the RFC Editor function after Postel died.
  • The Internet Society took over funding, which the US government had provided until 1998. USC/ISI was selected for 2007-2009, and 2009 would see a significant transition.
  • The editorial process became more efficient and transparent.
  • An RFC Editorial Board was formed, which helps review Independent Submission stream RFCs.
  • The email list rfc-interest@rfc-editor.org was created for community input.
sections.eli5: After the first caretaker died, friends kept the library going, new people paid for it, and a team and a mailing list were added for help and advice.

sections.title: Security and Thanks
sections.content: The memo says it raises no security issues. In its acknowledgments, USC/ISI says it has been an honor to serve the community for 31 years.
sections.eli5: Nothing in it can cause trouble. It ends with a thank you.

references.text: RFC Editor, et al., "30 Years of RFCs", RFC 2555, April 1999.
